title: Ram Charan Just Showed the World His Twins. Three Tiny Hands, Two Words, and the Internet Lost It.
excerpt: On their 14th anniversary, the Peddi star and Upasana broke their silence on Shivram and Anveera Devi — and proved you don't need to show a face to break the timeline.
body:
It was just three tiny hands. No faces, no nursery reveal, no glossy magazine spread. On the morning of June 14, **Ram Charan** and **Upasana Kamineni Konidela** posted a single photograph to Instagram — the hands of their three children laced together, the newborn twins' fingers curled beside the slightly older hand of their daughter Klin Kaara — and a caption of just two words: *"Heart is full,"* trailed by an infinity symbol.

Within minutes it had gone supernova. Two hundred thousand likes and climbing. **Kajal Aggarwal** and **Huma Qureshi** in the comments with hearts. A flood of *"No nazar"* from fans terrified the universe might be jealous of so much joy. For a couple who guard their family life like a state secret, this was the equivalent of pulling back a velvet curtain — just an inch, just enough.

> "Heart is full." — Upasana Kamineni Konidela

The twins, a boy and a girl, arrived on January 31, named **Shivram** and **Anveera Devi Konidela** in a private *naamkaran* in Hyderabad. It was Ram Charan's father, the legendary **Chiranjeevi**, who first told the world, posting that *"Shiva Ram is a profound confluence of two eternal ideals"* — Lord Shiva and Lord Rama, strength fused with compassion. Anveera, he explained, signifies a bravery that expands toward the limitless; the *"Devi"* deliberate, *"a reminder that strength and grace can co-exist."* Try finding a Bollywood baby name that comes with a thesis statement. You won't.



> **"A flood of *"No nazar"* from fans terrified the universe might be jealous of so much joy."**


What makes this reveal land so hard isn't the photograph. It's the timing. Charan is having the year of his life. **Peddi**, his sports drama with **Buchi Babu Sana**, has stormed past ₹157 crore worldwide and become the biggest South Indian film of 2026 — the same film that, eleven days before release, the trade was quietly writing off. He played a wrestler, a cricketer, three sporting avatars and a physical transformation that had casting directors texting in capitals. The man is, by every metric, on top of the mountain.

And instead of milking the victory lap, he posted his children's hands.

There's something quietly radical about that choice, especially for the diaspora reading from Edison or Hounslow or Brampton. We grew up on a film industry that treated star kids as currency — the dramatic hospital exits, the staged airport reveals, the magazine bidding wars. Charan and Upasana, who married in June 2012 after years as friends, have done the opposite at every turn. Klin Kaara arrived in June 2023 with the same restraint. The faces stay private. The love stays loud.

Upasana — vice-chairman of Apollo Charity, a force in her own right long before she became *"the RRR star's wife"* — has always understood the assignment better than most. During Diwali 2025 she teased the second pregnancy with a single line from her Seemantham ceremony: *"double the celebration, double the love and double the blessings."* Double, as it turned out, was literal.

For a generation of NRIs who watched **RRR** become the first Telugu film many of their American colleagues had ever heard of — who watched Charan and Jr NTR carry Naatu Naatu to the Oscars stage — there's a particular tenderness to seeing him pivot from global icon to a dad posting baby hands at sunrise. The crossover dream and the cradle, in the same news cycle.

Professionally, the road ahead is stacked: a long-rumoured collaboration with **Sukumar**, whispers of projects with **Trivikram Srinivas** and producer **Naga Vamsi**. Nothing locked, everything buzzing. The Mega family empire keeps expanding in every direction at once.

But for one Sunday in June, none of that was the headline. Three small hands were. And honestly? That's the flex. In an industry addicted to spectacle, the most magnetic thing Ram Charan did all year was show us almost nothing — and let us feel everything.

Klin Kaara, Shivram, Anveera. Heart full, indeed.
